name: Anarcho-Syndicalism
summary: Anarcho-syndicalism is the anarchist wing of revolutionary trade unionism. It holds that unions, organised from below and federated, should wage the class struggle by direct action and the general strike, then take over production themselves and replace both capitalism and the state. It rejects parliaments, political parties and any dictatorship, and is internationalist and anti-militarist.
scope: The classical movement as theorised by Rudolf Rocker (Anarcho-Syndicalism, 1938) and practised by Spain's CNT, using its 1936 Zaragoza resolution on libertarian communism as the programme. It excludes plain syndicalism without the anarchist goal of abolishing the state, and Marxist-influenced union strategies.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Free provision of needs is the goal, but through communes and producers' bodies rather than the state; inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wages are fought over by union direct action and the wage system is ultimately rejected, so a state-set minimum is not their remedy; inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Production and consumption are to be organised by labour councils and federations rather than competitive markets.

public-ownership.rationale: Industry is to be collectivised under workers' control by unions, not owned by the state, so public ownership in the usual sense is rejected.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: They seek to abolish capitalist property rather than tax it through a state they want gone; inferred.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are the vehicle of class struggle and the embryo of the new society.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Zaragoza resolution declares private property abolished after the revolution.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Reforms through state regulation are distrusted; the aim is workers taking over, not tighter rules; inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: They want needs met collectively, not cut, though through mutual provision rather than state welfare; inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Workers' control of production and distribution is the central economic aim.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Distrust of the state as defender of privilege makes expanded state surveillance unacceptable; inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Libertarian stance against state punishment and prisons; drug policy itself not addressed, so inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Opposed to state censorship in general, while fiercely anti-fascist in practice; inferred and contested.

strong-leader.rationale: Rocker rejects leaders, dictatorship and domination from above in favour of organisation from below.

state-harmful.rationale: Abolition of the state alongside capitalism is the stated goal.

limit-guns.rationale: The resolution favours an armed population ("the people armed") as protection of the revolution.

empower-police-military.rationale: The resolution calls a permanent army the greatest danger to the revolution.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The text proclaims free love by mutual consent but says nothing on sex work; adherents split.

decide-locally.rationale: Rocker wants free combination from below upward and calls centralism a curse.

rehabilitation.rationale: The resolution rejects prisons and punitive institutions and blames crime on social injustice.

traditional-family.rationale: The family is not attacked, but free love and equality of the sexes replace traditional authority structures.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Sexual freedom by mutual consent is endorsed, though state-sanctioned marriage is not their concern; inferred.

abortion-legal.rationale: Consistent with sexual freedom and equality of the sexes; not directly addressed, so inferred.

more-religion-public.rationale: Religion is tolerated only as private conscience, not public display or coercion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Opposition to domination and privilege implies support, though not a stated programme; inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The text ties women's dependence to capitalism and expects it to end with economic independence; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Rocker holds that workers' interests cross borders and distrusts the nation state and its cultural claims.

gradual-change.rationale: Revolutionary change, with violent convulsions where necessary, is expected, and existing institutions are not respected.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Class solidarity across borders is a core principle.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Internationalist, but organisations of states are state power; they favour federations of workers' bodies instead; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Rocker criticises the scramble for markets at workers' expense; free trade as such not addressed.

nation-first.rationale: Workers should not tie their efforts to national states.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Anti-militarist and hostile to state wars; the Zaragoza text allows armed defence of the revolution only; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Class interests cross borders and nation states are rejected.

limit-growth.rationale: The current favours industrialisation and large-scale industry; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed historically; collective control of production would allow it; inferred.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Favours industrial production under workers' control but Rocker also notes machines reduced workers to mechanism parts.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic, no principled position; adherents split.

revolution-justified.rationale: Rocker holds social transformation cannot come without violent revolutionary convulsions.

experts-over-public.rationale: Rocker warns against domination by bureaucratic mediocrity and stresses the creative energy of the masses.

central-planning.rationale: Coordination is by federations from below; centralism is rejected as a curse.

socialized-markets.rationale: Exchange is organised through councils, production cards and federations rather than markets; inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: A state tax scheme is foreign to their aims; land is to be collectivised; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance goes with private property to be abolished, but taxing it presupposes a state; adherents split.

basic-income.rationale: Distribution is tied to producers' contribution and need through their own bodies, not state payments; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Nationalist economic protection runs against internationalism; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Rocker rejects the state as defender of privilege and wants economic direction by labour councils.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Rocker supports collectivising land and other means of production, not spreading private ownership.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Libertarian communism aims at distribution by need; production cards and some wages are transitional.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: They would end the state and capital, but not leave money to a market; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies are the opposite of free federations independent of the state.

one-party-rule.rationale: Rocker says party dictatorship became the rule of a small clique over the proletariat.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Rocker holds that the state defends privilege; monarchy is its extreme form.

democracy-best.rationale: Parliamentary democracy is called a failed expression of capitalism, though assemblies and self-management are favoured.

direct-votes.rationale: Popular assemblies and councils settle matters; the text rejects parliament.

workers-councils.rationale: Rocker names a system of labour councils as the political form of Socialism.

right-to-secede.rationale: Communes are autonomous within a federation and may opt out of general agreements.

natural-rulers.rationale: Rocker wants 'government over men' to give way to the administration of economic affairs, implying no one is fit to rule others, though natural rulers are not discussed.

political-violence-never.rationale: Rocker accepts armed resistance in critical cases and violent upheaval as likely.

war-builds-character.rationale: Workers should refuse to serve the wars of the possessing classes.

separate-church-state.rationale: Religion is a private matter, and the state is abolished anyway.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Religion is limited to private conscience and authority of any kind is rejected.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The Zaragoza text puts defence in an armed population and justice in popular assemblies, not companies.

military-superiority.rationale: The CNT's Zaragoza programme warns that 'a permanent army would constitute the greatest danger to the revolution' and entrusts defence to the armed people and the communes.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Nationalism is rejected in favour of cross-border class solidarity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Class struggle awakens worker solidarity and is the method of revolution, though Rocker rejects economic determinism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Distribution by need and equal rights for all point toward material equality.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Autonomous communes and federalism suggest support; not directly addressed, so inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anti-imperialism is standard, but reparations are not discussed; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Unions of states or civilisations on religious lines contradict internationalism.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Solidarity and mutual agreement are the basis of their organisation.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Rocker puts individual freedom first within free agreement and rejects imposed collective claims.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: No explicit ecological position in the text; the naturist communes are tolerated; inferred.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; adherents split.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalism favours industrialisation, unlike primitivist currents.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Supports industry under workers' control, with no stated view on speeding up disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed; adherents split.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Decision-making is meant to rest on workers' councils from below; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Distrust of the state and surveillance implies support; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Revolutionary goals aim at a new society, not a lost one.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Rocker insists means must follow principle: socialism will be free or not at all.

direct-action.rationale: Strikes, boycotts and sabotage are used instead of legal channels and parliament.

means-match-ends.rationale: Rocker says socialism will be free or it will not be at all.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Favours industrial production under workers' control.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Unions are organised by industry and run production; the division of labour is not abolished as such; inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The resolution's first principle is giving each person what they need, though contribution is used transitionally.

production-for-use.rationale: Rocker contrasts cooperative labour serving needs with production for profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Rocker, drawing on Proudhon, sees property as the privilege of exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rocker calls it a frightful despotism that became a small clique's dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Rocker supports collectivising land, and rural collectives are discussed, though some communes opt out.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Rocker calls wars those of the possessing classes and criticises the scramble for markets.

taxation-theft.rationale: The state is seen as an exploiter but the theft framing is a property-rights one adherents do not use; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed as such; the state is rejected, so the principle is not a test for restricting adults.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Individuals are free within federated communities; rights are not framed as only individual; inferred.

conscription.rationale: Permanent armies and compulsion are rejected in favour of an armed population.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Rocker wants direct participation in councils, not exit as the main check; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is a defender of privilege to be abolished, not run like a business.

positive-liberty.rationale: Rocker says higher cultural life and freedom need a material standard of living first.

media-academia-power.rationale: Real power is held by capital and state; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Equality of rights and rejection of privilege; race science is not part of the doctrine.

organic-representation.rationale: Rejects parties but uses workplace councils and communes, not families or corporate bodies.

total-state.rationale: Rocker says state and culture are irreconcilable opposites.

national-rebirth.rationale: Rocker opposes nationalism and fascism's drive to bring all life under the state, implying rejection of national rebirth, which he does not discuss as such.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Rejects the state and nationalism; Rocker criticises seizing markets at others' cost.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rejecting every form of political power and privilege excludes feudal loyalty, though Rocker does not discuss oaths of fealty.

bound-labor.rationale: Rocker praises the uprisings of feudal bondmen peasants for preparing the abolition of feudal privileges, treating serfdom as domination to be overthrown.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed; education is to be scientific and free, which cuts both ways.

universal-morality.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; adherents split.

single-common-good.rationale: Rocker criticises the abstract general will and favours free agreement among groups.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Opposition to nation states implies rejection; not directly addressed.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Free movement is favoured but citizenship in a national homeland is a state concept; inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: Nationalist projects run against their internationalism; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workers run plants through labour councils elected by them.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education is to be free and equal, run collectively, not marketed; inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: State fiscal policy is outside their programme; adherents split.

economic-freedom.rationale: Rocker says political rights need an economic basis, though the meaning differs from market freedom; inferred.

rule-by-example.rationale: Authority itself is rejected in favour of free agreement; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Workers should not tie themselves to national states; free communes are the unit instead.

force-without-un.rationale: Opposes wars of states and militarism.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Education is scientific and religion private; not stated as a principle, so inferred.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Class solidarity across borders rejects citizenship-based exclusion.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Each is asked to give their maximum contribution, but not through state conditions; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Class struggle through unions is the method; collaboration is rejected.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Rocker values culture and calls for a material base for it, not its destruction.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-imperialist but wary of state-led fronts; inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: Rocker says workers' solidarity 'must reach beyond the artificial boundaries of the states' and that labour must not tie its efforts 'with the interests of the national states'.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The text declares the sexes equal in rights and responsibilities.

ban-interest.rationale: They would abolish capital and money lending but not by state law; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Zaragoza programme's aim of ending all divisions between oppressors and oppressed implies rejecting racial segregation; it does not mention race.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Rocker calls the state the defender of mass exploitation and social privileges.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Cross-border solidarity and rejection of nationalism make cultural assimilation demands foreign.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy of this kind is not part of the doctrine, which stresses class solidarity across borders.

proportional-representation.rationale: Parliamentary activity is called weak and hopeless, though PR is a reform within it; inferred.

national-mission.rationale: Rocker condemns socialists who backed annexations in the World War and opposes national states, implying rejection of any national mission abroad.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The text ties women's dependence to capitalism and demands equal rights.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Rocker says party ambition for power corrupted Socialism.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Anti-state and anti-police, but a legal accountability mechanism is not their approach; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Rocker calls the state 'capable only of protecting old privileges and creating new ones' and 'the defender of mass exploitation and social privileges', so a state that protects property is what he rejects.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Equality of rights and rejection of privilege.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The text declares the sexes equal in rights and responsibilities and rejects privilege.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Internationalism, class interests cross borders; the claim is inferred.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The state is rejected; equality before the law is not the question for them.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Religion is for individual conscience, which excludes coercion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; opposed to religious law by state; inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Education is to be free, scientific and equal; religion is private.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Rocker rejects the idea that the state withers after being strengthened.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Free agreement from below is their principle, though they reject the state altogether; inferred.

trade-surplus.rationale: Rocker criticises seizing markets at others' cost; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Cross-border solidarity and rejection of coercive state power.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Rocker, following Kropotkin, stresses cooperation and solidarity; inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Opposed to state censorship but also to parties; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Opposition to arbitrary power is central, though the term is theirs by inference.

separated-powers.rationale: They would abolish the state rather than balance it; federations of councils replace it.

vanguard-party.rationale: Rocker says a party speaking for a class becomes a clique's dictatorship.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Distribution by need favours the poor; not stated as a priority rule; inferred.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Private property in housing is not their aim; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The strike and the general strike are the central weapons.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Poverty arises from exploitation and privilege.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Delegates are elected for single terms and paid like workers; lottery is not mentioned.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Rocker defends rights as habit defended by the people and distrusts state power.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: A state price system is foreign to them; distribution by councils; inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Rocker condemns Bolshevik rule as 'the dictatorship of a small clique', implying opposition to party control of information, though he does not discuss the press.

party-commands-army.rationale: Rocker rejects party dictatorship; permanent army is rejected.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Rocker accepts violent upheaval and armed resistance as part of revolution, and their goals do not rest on non-aggression.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Wikipedia notes delegates serve single terms and are paid the same as the workers they represent.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists reject political parties as such, while holding that union members honor agreed decisions; inferred on parties as the statement frames them.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Rocker rejects the state and nationalism and favors federation from below, so a bureaucratic union like the EU is opposed; inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The movement rejects the state and standing armies in favor of an armed population, so a head of state commanding the military is opposed.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The CNT program and Rocker reject church authority and hierarchy.

clerical-rule.rationale: The CNT program and Rocker reject religious authority over society and the state.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Rocker holds that militarism and war serve ruling classes, and the movement is internationalist and anti-militarist.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The movement rejects state coercion over thought and culture and favors free education; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The movement has no presidents, and delegates serve single short terms; the statement presumes an office it opposes, so inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Delegates are mandated and revocable by the bodies that send them in the federal union structure.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists are outspoken opponents of nationalist ambitions and militarism and fight war through anti-militarist propaganda and strikes.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The 1936 program socialized housing through the communes, so landlords go, but the model is communal provision rather than family ownership; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: Rocker opposed standing armies and the CNT raised militias in 1936; no program for an armed citizenry is stated, so inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed; the program federates communes of towns and villages without favoring either.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Rocker describes the movement as hostile to all nationalist ambitions, so it would not seek to unify nations in states.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The movement distrusts intellectual leaders but the 1936 program stresses universal education; adherents are split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Internationalism and opposition to nationalism imply no culture is ranked above others; inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: The Zaragoza program declares libertarian communism incompatible with punitive justice, abolishing prisons, and attributes crime to social causes.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The Zaragoza program calls for free, scientific education equal for both sexes, with sex education beginning at school.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The program wants scientific education and confines religion to private conscience, so creationism in schools is excluded.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The program is silent on pornography; its libertarian stance against coercive institutions suggests opposing legal restriction.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The movement rejects nationalism and the state, so state citizenship by descent is not its rule; inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Autonomous federated communes imply respect for local languages and cultures; not stated, so inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The program recognizes religion only as private conscience and rejects special public standing, so legal exemptions are unlikely to be sought; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The program aims at developing the individualities of children and people; inferred as agreement.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists oppose capitalist exploitation internationally and would reject debt owed to financiers, though the sources read do not mention it; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Rocker holds that political freedom from the state means little without ending capitalist ownership, and criticises nationalism as serving ruling classes.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Rocker rejects parliaments and the state and favours federated labour councils, so a state constituent assembly is not their route.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists reject dictatorship and any state coercion in the name of development, as Rocker condemns the Bolshevik path.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Rocker's internationalism and solidarity suggest support for helping the poor abroad, though through workers' organisations rather than states; inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Rocker rejects the state and militarism, and the CNT programme speaks of an armed population rather than a standing army.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Rocker rejects the state, parliament and parties, so a president elected by the people has no place.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists abolish state control of money and want producers' federations to run the economy, so neither option fits; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Rocker rejects nationalism and the national state, and the movement is internationalist.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The Zaragoza programme puts production and property in common ownership for the needs of all.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Rocker condemns Bolshevism as a state dictatorship over workers that kept hierarchy and wage labour.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The sources are silent on environmental precaution; no position follows from the programme.

collective-defense.rationale: Rocker opposes militarism and nationalism, and the CNT favoured an armed population in place of standing armies and alliances.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Rocker opposes the nation-state and conquest while backing peoples' freedom; inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The CNT programme rejects religion's power and aims to abolish the state, so state control of churches is not their remedy; inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Rocker rejects the state and its offices and parties in favour of federated labour bodies.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Rocker's federalism builds from voluntary association from below and rejects the coercive nation-state.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The CNT envisaged autonomous communes in a free federation; inferred for a region keeping its own system.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Rocker rejects the state and all forms of rule, and the CNT programme rejects religious authority.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The state-set tax system is rejected with the state; a flat rate is the less egalitarian form; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Rocker stresses that social conditions shape human development; inferred as a lean to nurture.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rocker opposes any rule above the people, which a sovereign above law embodies.

space-expansion.rationale: The sources do not address space policy.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Rocker rejects government by the few and parliamentary rule in favour of federated councils.

leader-cult.rationale: Rocker rejects dictatorship, leader worship and authority from above.

equal-parenting.rationale: The CNT programme addresses family and education but not custody rules; no clear position.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists rejected party dictatorship and held that bureaucracies could become a new ruling class; inferred.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Zaragoza program calls for expropriating land and its collective use by the working peasants.

refugee-return.rationale: Internationalism and opposition to borders imply a right of return; inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Rocker's anarcho-syndicalism is internationalist and rejects nationalism.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The movement was secular and strongly anticlerical.

women-must-cover.rationale: Libertarian communism opposes compulsion in personal life; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Libertarian communism aims at ending money and capitalist finance; inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalism is internationalist and opposes unity by nationality.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Federalism from below allows cultural self-government within a federation; inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Workers' internationalism urges struggle for equality where one lives; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Rocker criticised Marxist economic determinism; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: The aim is to replace capitalism through union control, not regulate competition; inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: Unions oppose rescuing capital with public money; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists reject state institutions and majority rule imposed through them; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Women's groups such as Mujeres Libres existed, but quotas in public bodies are not a stated program; no settled position.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The movement is internationalist and opposes closed economic blocs and colonialism.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists reject state trade agreements; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Libertarian communism rests on solidarity and producers' self-management more than wages; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The strategy is the mass general strike and union action, not a small armed group.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Libertarian communism abolishes class privilege, including inherited rank.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Rocker rejects nationalism as a tool of the state and the movement is internationalist, so a nation-centred curriculum is disfavoured; inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rocker condemns the state and national domination and the movement is anti-imperialist, so one society ruling another for its good is rejected.

patriotic-education.rationale: Rocker sees nationalism and the state's claim on loyalty as tools of power, and the CNT programme demands education free of state and church control.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The movement stands for equality of all people but did not address state admissions or hiring preferences; adherents would split; inferred.

public-money-creation.rationale: The Zaragoza programme replaces money with production cards and communal distribution, so neither state nor bank money creation is endorsed; inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The movement holds that capitalism will be ended by the workers' revolution and general strike rather than lasting indefinitely; not addressed directly, so inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Rocker opposes nationalism, power politics and the state's expansion, so cultivating influence over a predecessor empire's lands is rejected.

delink-world-market.rationale: The movement is internationalist and federalist and seeks cooperation across borders, though it rejects capitalist trade; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalism rests on workers of all countries sharing class interests and being exploited, so the claim is disfavoured; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The movement's equality of all people and rejection of domination mean it would not defend discrimination by owners; the CNT also rejects private property in production.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rocker views constitutions and the state as instruments of ruling classes and holds freedom comes from social struggle rather than written guarantees; inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Internationalist and anti-imperialist, so imposed colonial borders would carry no legitimacy; inferred from that outlook.

elective-rulers.rationale: Rejects hereditary rule as plainly as any other, but wants no rulers at all, only recallable delegates; inferred, so the agreement is partial.

minority-veto.rationale: Federal free agreement stresses voluntary association and the right to withdraw, but union decisions are taken by majority; adherents split.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Resistance to any ruler is taken for granted and goes further than the statement, which presupposes a legitimate constitutional ruler; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Rocker calls parliamentary activity the weakest form of struggle and rejects parliaments and parties as instruments of emancipation.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Anarchist thought has often extended solidarity to animals, but the sources do not take this up; inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Adherents split between vegetarian abolitionists and those who accept humane use; the sources are silent.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Rocker puts mutual aid and workers' own action in place of the patronage of the privileged, who are seen as an exploiting class; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Rocker's movement demands active participation in social struggle and self-management, although it rejects parliamentary politics.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Rocker's critique of state and church holds that they dull the people's will to resist, which extends naturally to media; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Rocker holds that state, church and education bind people to the existing order alongside coercion; inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Internationalist and anti-capitalist, so global exploitation by rich states and firms fits, though the classical sources focus on class within nations; inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Rocker rejects nationalism, and the movement is internationalist and wants no state offices to reserve in the first place.

party-own-road.rationale: The CNT refused direction from Moscow, but anarcho-syndicalism rejects parties altogether, so the statement only half applies; inferred.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Not addressed; mutual aid and federation suggest cooperation rather than strict self-reliance, but they also oppose capitalist loans; split.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Rocker rejects nationalism and the movement is internationalist and anti-militarist, so territorial claims are rejected.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Opposes rule by any group by birth, though it supports indigenous self-management and decolonisation; inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The CNT fought fascism in 1936, but the movement rejects constitutions, so a founding-value clause only partly fits; inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Rocker condemns Bolshevik dictatorship alongside fascism, and the movement was crushed by both Franco and Stalinists.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Scholarship holds slavery was the central cause and anti-slavery egalitarianism points the same way; inferred, not argued in the sources.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Hostile to symbols of state and military glory, so adherents would not defend them, though some prefer contextualising to removal; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Equal concern for people's needs would extend to boys and men, though the sources are silent; inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Opposes all domination and violence, so equal services would be supported, though many would stress it is gendered; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Internationalist and universalist about freedom and self-management, though it also values local variation; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Rocker's movement is anti-militarist and rejects any standing army or military power.

paid-care-work.rationale: Libertarian communism provides for all needs and labour recognition, but the sources do not mention domestic work; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: The 1936 programme treats the family as a free union, so imposed lifelong duties are doubtful; inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Rocker rejects the state and its officialdom in favour of producers' councils, so examined officials are not their model; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: They oppose capitalism and the state, and do not look to state intervention to protect firms; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The CNT programme treats relationships as free unions, so ending a marriage needs no fault; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Delegates serve a single term, are paid as workers and can be recalled, which matches mandated delegation.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The programme replaces wages with distribution by need under communes, so private pension accounts are rejected.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The 1936 resolution places land and production in the communes and producers' bodies; the nation is not their unit.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Rocker calls parliamentary activity the weakest form of struggle, but a legislative check on spending is not something they would defend; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Rocker rejects nationalism and state culture, so an enforced national language is opposed; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Rocker's internationalism rejects nationalist limits on foreigners; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists oppose racism but would fight it through union action rather than state review; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Their picture of production for need rather than profit points against consumerism; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: They are anti-militarist and oppose states, so state sponsorship of insurgents is rejected; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Rocker attacks militarism, imperialism and Bolshevik domination, so military intervention within a bloc is rejected.

corporate-influence.rationale: Rocker treats the state and capitalism as intertwined, so capital's hold on government is expected, though the remedy is revolution; inferred.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists oppose the state and nationalism, so they do not support state control of funding; inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Rocker rejects nationalism and state interference; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: The CNT programme puts land and housing under communes, not local authorities limiting purchases; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: The programme abolishes wage labour and replaces the state with producers' bodies, so a state job guarantee is not their goal; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: Rocker treats states as militaristic and opposes the idea of spreading democracy through state means; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Rocker rejects the state's authority and its law as instruments of ruling-class power, so no general duty to obey the law.

non-intervention.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists oppose states, but supported international solidarity as in the Spanish Civil War; adherents would split.

industrial-unions.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalism organises workers in industrial federations of unions, as the CNT did, rather than by craft.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Rocker rejects nationalism and racism in favour of internationalism.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The CNT programme recognises free union of couples without state or church involvement, so state-conferred marriage is unneeded; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Rocker opposes state secrecy as instrument of domination, though the movement does not campaign for legal rights; inferred.

local-production.rationale: The CNT programme has communes federated and exchanging goods, so local production is partial but not a stated principle.

informal-organisation.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalism relies on permanent federated unions, not informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists reject the state's constitution and law and are internationalist; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: The CNT programme rejects religion and Rocker rejects nationalism, so a nation defined by religion contradicts it.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Rocker rejects hierarchy among states and peoples, so ritual submission to a leading power has no place; inferred from his anti-state internationalism.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Communes and unions federate and share by need rather than hoard local revenue; inferred from the distribution-by-need programme.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The libertarian-communist programme socialises production, land and tools, not personal belongings; inferred from its production-and-distribution scheme.

defeat-communism.rationale: Rocker fiercely opposes Bolshevism, but anti-militarism and rejection of state power make a state campaign to defeat communism unlikely; inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Services are to be run by producers and communes, with no room for private profit-making providers; inferred from the programme.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Zaragoza programme and Rocker treat the church as an instrument of domination and expect religion to wane; the consolation thesis is inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists see capitalism as a stage that concentrated production but stress its exploitation; adherents are split and the sources do not settle it.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Zaragoza programme calls for equality of the sexes inside a new social order; inferred that this is tied to abolishing wage labour.

socialized-care.rationale: Communal organisation of consumption and care is in keeping with libertarian communism; inferred, not stated in the sources read.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Rocker is hostile to nationalism and state cultural policy, so official linguistic purges would be rejected; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Rocker opposes the domination of peoples by states, so unilateral cancellation of obligations would be rejected; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The programme is built on federated free communes owning means of production in common.

majority-settlement.rationale: Rocker rejects nationalism and state policy to assimilate peoples, so state-steered settlement is opposed.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Rocker rejects both capitalism and Bolshevik state communism in favour of federal, union-run socialism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Anarchists are internationalist and reject nations and states as the bearers of rights, so a people's tie to land does not outrank the claims of those living there now.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Committed anti-fascists accept the historical record of the genocide and have no motive to deny it; the sources do not discuss it, so this is inferred from their anti-fascism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Rejecting state coercion over personal life and the criminal law as an instrument of authority, adherents oppose criminalising consensual relations.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Suppressing opposition is the practice of the state and dictatorship that the ideology rejects, and it criticised the Bolsheviks for exactly this.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Adherents are anti-clerical and oppose any state enforcing religion; punishing blasphemy would be authority at its worst.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Anti-imperialism and internationalism follow from rejecting exploitation and the state; colonial rule for the ruler's benefit is exploitation.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Adherents back resistance to invasion but not a religious obligation, which they would not recognise; inferred from their secular, anti-religious stance.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Adherents accept overthrowing rulers but not on the ground of failing to apply religious law, since they reject religious authority; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Direct self-management by those affected, in workplaces and communities through federated assemblies, is the core of the ideology's alternative to the state.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Class struggle through unions is the focus and adherents are split between that and broader modern framings; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Opposition to hierarchy and discrimination suggests support for protection, though classical sources never address it and adherents may distrust state legal recognition; inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: Individual autonomy over one's own life points to support, though the classical sources do not discuss it; inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The ideology sits firmly on the revolutionary left and sees capitalists and workers as opposed classes whose best ideas cannot be merged.

alienated-labor.rationale: Wage labour is condemned as wage slavery that cuts workers off from the product and control of their work, and free creative work is the aim.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Adherents reject cultural essentialism, racism and scapegoating of minorities, even while criticising religion generally; inferred from internationalism.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Atheism and the rejection of all authority are central, as in Bakunin's anarchist critique of God and the state.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Adherents are anti-clerical but oppose state compulsion over personal dress and want no state institutions at all; inferred, and views vary.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Adherents back workers' protection against employer power, though the sources do not address this legal tool; inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: Both markets and wage relations are rejected, and the state-regulated compromise is rejected as well; production and distribution are to be organised in common.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Anti-militarism is central and the standing army is rejected, but the movement organised its own militias in 1936; so agreement is strong but not total.

rich-first.rationale: Equality and abolition of class privilege are central; letting some get rich first contradicts them.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Anti-militarism and rejection of rival states point to refusing alignment with great-power blocs, though adherents would prefer no state armies at all.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists reject the state and all hereditary authority; Rocker treats monarchy and privilege as products of power to be abolished.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Rocker draws on Proudhon's mutualism, so cost-price credit from user-owned banks fits their outlook better than profit banks, but it is not a union programme point; inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: They oppose capitalist finance and would back refusing imposed austerity, though they look to workers' action rather than governments; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: Rocker rejects parliamentary politics and class privilege, so a property qualification on voting is opposed on both counts.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Anti-authoritarian principles extend to opposing domination generally, but the classical sources do not link women and nature; inferred.

reification.rationale: Rocker and the CNT treat wage labour as subordinating people to capital, close to the idea of economic forces ruling people, though the term is not used; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists hold that political freedoms are empty under capitalism, and they built their own union press because the owners' press was closed to them.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: They reject state rule and legislation, so the statement's premise of rulers governing is not their position, though they prefer it to arbitrary decrees; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalism is internationalist and organises workers regardless of race, so it opposes ethnic limits on rights.

online-participation.rationale: Direct participation through federated assemblies is central, but the classical sources say nothing about the internet and adherents would be split on parliamentary-style deliberation; inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: They would favour open records while any public administration exists, though their aim is to replace the state; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The movement was strongly anticlerical and opposed state and church control of private life, so it rejects legal limits on marriage.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The boycott is a syndicalist tool against employers, but an internationalist movement would reject its use against a religious minority.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Decisions belong to union assemblies and mandated, recallable delegates, not to a lot-chosen body deciding for everyone; inferred from the federal, assembly-based structure the sources describe.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The movement was strongly anti-clerical and treated religion as an illusion to be overcome, not a doctrine to be updated, while also rejecting fixed clerical authority; inferred from its secularism.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists see capitalist ownership as the root of class domination and want productive wealth held by the unions and communes, so concentrated wealth is a threat to liberty.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the anti-discrimination, free-association spirit of the movement; the sources do not discuss military service, and they are anti-militarist.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The movement wants the state abolished, so a state programme of promoting atheism conflicts with its principles, even though the CNT and many members were anticlerical.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from the aim of abolishing the state and its coercive apparatus in favour of communes and producers' federations; the sources do not detail policing.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred: they reject state executives entirely and favour federated communes and union delegates rather than power-sharing between communities.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred: they favour solidarity through the union and commune as of right rather than charity.

term-limits.rationale: Wikipedia notes that delegates serve single terms and are paid the same as the workers they represent, which is rotation of office.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from delegates being mandated and recallable by the union base; the sources do not discuss delegation by policy area.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The classical movement predates the issue and no stated position makes it a top priority; inferred indifference.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from equality of the sexes in their libertarian-communist programme; the sources do not discuss churches.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from their opposition to authority in all relations and equality of the sexes; the sources do not discuss marriage.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Rocker's internationalism treats workers of every nationality as one class, so adherents would let long-term residents vote locally; inferred, though they also reject parliamentary voting itself.

rent-control.rationale: The Zaragoza programme puts housing under communal control and ends rent for profit, so capping rents in the meantime fits; inferred.

abolish-ip.rationale: Libertarian communism ends private ownership of the means of production and distributes by need, which fits freely copyable ideas; the sources do not mention patents, so inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Rocker rejects nationalism, militarism and state-run organisation of the young, so drilled youth movements for national service are the opposite of the programme.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Rocker's anti-militarism and rejection of the state's armed power make stationing nuclear weapons on any territory unacceptable.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The movement is anti-militarist and internationalist and opposes state armies, so foreign bases are opposed, though not in the language of national sovereignty.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Adherents condemn mass killing but distrust official state declarations; no source addresses formal recognition, so this is a genuine split inferred from principles.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Zaragoza programme replaces property income with production cards for useful work and abolishes rent and interest as unearned.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The programme calls for an armed population to defend the revolution and Rocker accepts defensive revolutionary force, so adherents do not hold that all killing is wrong.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Rocker argues that nations are products of the state and of ruling-class interests, not a continuous ancient essence.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The tradition is class-centred and never addresses the sex/gender debate; adherents would split, inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The movement organises by class and industry and has no stated position on feminist identity politics; adherents are split, inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Rocker rejects nationalism and the cult of the nation, so sacralising the national dead is rejected.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The Zaragoza programme is materialist and treats religion as a private matter, and Rocker sees politics as class struggle, not a cosmic one.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Rocker's rejection of the nation-state and nationalism leaves no role for a national homeland as a spiritual centre; inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: Rocker holds that the state creates the nation rather than the reverse and that culture grows from free communities; inferred that culture precedes any state.

god-not-male.rationale: Religion is a private matter in the programme and anarcho-syndicalists are largely secular; adherents are indifferent, inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Adherents are hostile to religious authority and the programme calls for equal rights for women, so setting aside texts that diminish women is acceptable; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Rocker's internationalism and class view reject tying economic life to national majority groups.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Rocker favours federations of free communities formed by voluntary choice, so borders are decided locally rather than by a fixed rule; inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: Rocker holds that unions must stay independent of parties and the state, and the profile's own missing statement records the same position.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Rocker treats socialism without workers' own self-management as state capitalism, though he wants workers to hold power through councils and unions rather than a political state.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The Zaragoza programme has communes and syndicates run services such as health and education collectively, which is public ownership without the state.

second-chamber.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists reject parliament altogether, so adding a chamber to it would not appeal; inferred from Rocker's view of parliamentary politics.

municipal-property.rationale: The Zaragoza programme makes the commune the basic unit that holds and administers productive property alongside the syndicates, rather than private owners or a national state.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Rocker's federalism builds from local bodies upward with delegates who coordinate and carry out decisions made below, which the statement describes.

family-wage.rationale: Distribution by need in the Zaragoza programme suggests support for pay that covers a household; the sources do not discuss wages for families, so this is inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: The movement never addressed drug regulation and its principles give no clear lean either way; inferred indifference.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: The movement never addressed life-extension research; its support for socialised health care gives no clear lean on this specific priority.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Hostility to state control and surveillance suggests sympathy for payments beyond state reach, though the programme abolishes money; inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: Rocker's opposition to state coercion and surveillance points to favouring anonymous online participation; anachronistic, so inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: Rocker puts the free development of the individual against the state's claims and sees the state as the enemy of personal liberty.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Rocker stresses culture and the free development of personality while the Zaragoza programme rejects organised religion, so adherents are split on this wording.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Federal autonomy for communes is meant to come from below and not be a grant from a national legislature, which anarcho-syndicalists reject as an authority.

gm-crops.rationale: The classical movement never addressed genetic engineering and its principles give no clear lean; inferred indifference.

dense-cities.rationale: The anarchist tradition behind the movement favoured decentralised communes joining town and country; inferred, not stated in the sources.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Rocker rejects nationalism and group identity as divisions that serve rulers, and organises on class lines.

racial-pride.rationale: Rocker rejects nationalist and racial pride as an ideology of rulers; inferred from his critique of nationalism.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The movement is anti-militarist and opposes wars of states, while the Zaragoza programme keeps an armed population to defend the revolution.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Rocker argues the nation is the result of the state rather than its cause, and the movement is internationalist, so a nation defined by language and history is rejected.

communal-electorates.rationale: They reject parliament and elections and treat religion as private, so religious separate electorates are firmly opposed.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Rocker criticises nationalism and national defence as tools of ruling classes, so claims of plots against the country are dismissed.

free-public-college.rationale: The Zaragoza programme calls for universal education for all, though run by communes and unions rather than the state.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: they want production run by unions and communes on need, not state taxes, so a tax-based approach is not theirs.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the aim of a lasting society planned for common welfare; the sources do not discuss ecology.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from their insistence on equality of the sexes in the Zaragoza programme, against fixed gender roles.

arms-reduction.rationale: Rocker condemns militarism and the CNT opposes standing armies, so lowering arms agrees in direction even though they reject national safety as the test.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred: they oppose state diplomacy, but of the kind that exists they would condemn secret agreements.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred: they aim at socialising capital via unions, not at state regulation of its flows.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists reject the state, and the CNT organised armed workers' militias in 1936.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Rocker's anti-militarism calls for refusing war service and for general strikes against war.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Unions are the core of the movement, though they pursue direct action and abolition of wage labour rather than negotiated contracts as the end.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: State top-ups keep the wage system and state in place; inferred.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: They want to abolish the state, not limit its borrowing; inferred.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Internationalist and anti-imperialist, but aimed at replacing capitalism by federated producers' bodies; inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Rocker holds the state must be replaced by federated workers' organisations, not taken over by parties.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Zaragoza sets out a fairly detailed libertarian-communist programme, but one built on voluntary federation and local autonomy; inferred split.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from opposition to turning everything into a commodity.

sacred-nation.rationale: Rocker criticises nationalism as a tool of the state and the movement is internationalist and secular.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from solidarity with working people against creditors, though through direct action rather than the state.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Federalism and rejection of central power imply that cores can dominate regions; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Rocker stresses human freedom and social development rather than a fixed nature; not directly addressed, adherents split.

public-service-media.rationale: They favour worker-run media outside the state; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Rocker was strongly secular and critical of church power; inferred, as the sources do not discuss comparative religion.

farm-price-support.rationale: The Zaragoza programme envisions agrarian communes and cooperatives federated by producers rather than state price guarantees; inferred.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists are anti-militarist and oppose the state; inferred from Rocker.

workers-own-party.rationale: Rocker argues party participation drained socialism of its creative force and calls parliamentary activity the weakest form of struggle, favouring unions instead.

ban-fgm.rationale: Opposition to domination of women is assumed, though enforcement by the state would be disliked; inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Equal rights for women are assumed, while inheritance and private land are to be socialised; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The sources do not address language naming, and the ideology is indifferent to it.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Producers' councils and communes would manage such harm collectively rather than through private suits or state agencies; inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalism rejects hierarchical lawmaking bodies in favour of federated delegates; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The sources do not address this tradeoff, and adherents would likely say free federations need not sacrifice either; treated as split.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists reject state punishment and the courts of the state; inferred from Rocker's critique of the state.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Internationalism and rejection of state compulsion mean they would not require this of newcomers; inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists want mass, solidaristic unions but reject coercion in principle; they never discuss mandatory dues, so this is inferred from that tension.

voter-id.rationale: Voting is not the movement's method, and state identity checks as a gate on political participation cut against its anti-state outlook; inferred.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Rocker opposes state churches and clerical power, so no interpretation of a religion should hold legal privilege.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The movement rejects parliamentary politics as domination and defines real self-rule as direct, federated control from below, not periodic elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: The anarchist tradition around the CNT, including its women's groups, rejected church-imposed sexual morality; the sources do not address it directly, so inferred.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: State suppression of communication is opposed on anti-state principle, though the technology is anachronistic for the classical movement; inferred.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The goal is distribution by communes and producers' bodies rather than a state cash scheme, so folding welfare into a state payment is unlikely to appeal; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: Adherents reject parliamentary voting itself but demand full equality of women, so would not limit rights to men; inferred.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalism is strongly anticlerical, so most adherents would blame church institutions for women's subordination, though the sources do not say so on gender; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: Rocker's writing rejects racial theories of peoples and nations, but the exact claim is not stated in the sources; inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Equality is to come from self-organised bodies, not new state ministries, which the movement would not set up; inferred.

missingStatements.text: A general strike is the best way to bring down capitalism.
missingStatements.rationale: Rocker calls the general strike a political action of greater importance than parliamentary proceedings, and Wikipedia names it as the key moment of revolution.

missingStatements.text: Trade unions should remain independent of all political parties.
missingStatements.rationale: Rocker argues party participation drained socialism of its creative force and calls parliamentary activity the weakest form of struggle.

missingStatements.text: Elected representatives should be paid no more than an average worker.
missingStatements.rationale: Wikipedia notes that delegates serve single terms and are paid the same as the workers they represent.

notes: The CNT joined the Republican government in 1936, which was controversial within the anarcho-syndicalist international. Distribution is disputed: some supporters keep contribution-based pay in a transition, others stress need. Ecology, religion and money are thinly covered by the sources read.
